_description: Hand-verified ground-truth set: every labelled particle in the three Material analysis report PDFs. This is the ONLY real labelled data available and is the primary verification gate for the prediction engine.
_provenance: Values transcribed verbatim from the PDF text layer (pdftotext / PyMuPDF). No value is computed, rounded or inferred. `chemistry` and `probable_source` are the analyst's own words from the report's Particle Details block.
_why_not_extracted: eds_extractor.py cannot currently parse these tables: _tokens_with_positions() splits on runs of 2+ spaces, but these reports separate narrow columns by a SINGLE space, so 'In stats. C', 'Cr Cu' and 'Sn Total' merge into single tokens and fail element lookup. Independently, the numeric values are not column-aligned with their headers in the text layer, so position-anchored slicing mis-assigns them. Both are pre-existing defects, verified by an old-vs-new behavioural diff. Until ingest is repaired this fixture is transcribed by hand.
_missing_semantics: A blank cell in the PDF means the element was NOT ANALYSED / not reported for that spectrum. It is recorded here by OMITTING the key, never as 0.0. Elements listed in `not_measured` were blank in that spectrum's row while present as a column in the table.
_units: weight percent, as printed. Processing option for every table: 'All elements analysed (Normalised)', so each spectrum sums to ~100%.

particles.source_pdf: Field CRI.I. 26-108 Particle In IC Stud (ISUZU) ......14.pdf
particles.notes: Mn 0.28-0.34 wt%. The shipped engine returns 'Sealing Ring' at confidence 1.00 for spectrum 1, matching on the Zn coating trace and trace Mn. Zn here is a surface coating ('Traces of Zn' per the report), not an alloy constituent.

particles.source_pdf: Field CRI.I. 26-108 Particle In IC Stud (ISUZU) ......14.pdf
particles.notes: CRITICAL CASE. Cr and Ni are NOT in this table at all - they were never analysed. The shipped engine returns 'Magnet housing' at confidence 1.00 (rule: S<=0.27 AND Mn>=1.39 AND Si>=0.33). Magnet housing is X8CrNiS18-9 austenitic stainless requiring Cr~17.8 and Ni~8.1 wt%; the rule checks neither. Correct behaviour: austenitic grades must be UNEVALUABLE here, never matched.

particles.source_pdf: Field CRI.I. 26-130 NB Seat Area Particle & Ball Damage (M&M) ....11.pdf
particles.notes: The report source list carries '??' - the analyst is explicitly uncertain between Magnet Nut and NR nut. The system must reproduce that ambiguity as a candidate SET, not launder it into a single confident answer. Note C ranges 3.81-15.82 wt% across one particle: strong evidence for metal-basis renormalisation.

particles.source_pdf: Field CRI.I. 26-130 NB Seat Area Particle & Ball Damage (M&M) ....11.pdf
particles.notes: Same material as 26-130-site1, measured on a different particle. Useful for multi-spectrum pooling: 7 spectra across the two sites should sharpen the estimate rather than being majority-voted.

particles.source_pdf: Field CRI.I. 26-130 NB Seat Area Particle & Ball Damage (M&M) ....11.pdf
particles.expected_family: F2 low-alloy Cr bearing steel (100Cr6) or Cr-Ni steel
particles.expected_behaviour: This is damage on a component surface, not a separate particle, and the report assigns no chemistry. An explicit abstention / needs-review is an acceptable and arguably correct answer. A confident single-component answer is NOT.
particles.notes: Cr 2.14 with Ni 1.95 gives Cr/Ni ~ 1.1, which is NOT the ~2.0-2.4 of austenitic 18/8 and not plain 100Cr6 either (100Cr6 carries no deliberate Ni). The shipped engine returns 'Unknown' here, which is the one case out of five it does not get confidently wrong.

particles.source_pdf: Field  CRI.I. 26-146 Particle In Z Hole Sr.No-2702 (M&M) ....22.pdf
particles.expected_family: F6 Cu-Sn bronze / metal matrix composite
particles.notes: HARDEST NORMALISATION CASE: C+O+F is ~75 wt% of the as-measured total (PTFE-loaded seal ring), leaving only ~24 wt% metal. Fe is absent entirely. On a metal basis Sn/Cu = 0.107, inside the CuSn bronze band, and that ratio is the signature that identifies this particle. The shipped engine returns 'HP Sealing' at confidence 1.00 by matching Cr 0.37-0.63 AND Mn<=0.0 - it never examines Cu or Sn, because no rule references either element.
